title: Registration and device-enrollment data can identify the homeowner
description: The flow carries account-registration details and enrolled camera/sensor identifiers to the Home Hub. These data can directly identify the homeowner or make them identifiable through account credentials, contact details, device serial numbers, and household-specific device inventory.
assumptions: Assumes the registration payload includes personal account data and device identifiers tied to a specific household.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context gives applicable threat types for this interaction but not detailed subtree ids.

title: Enrollment traffic may enable linkage between homeowner identity and household devices
description: By combining account-registration data with camera/sensor enrollment information, the Home Hub can link a named or otherwise identifiable homeowner to a specific set of devices and therefore to a particular home environment. This creates a privacy risk if the linkage is unnecessary, overly broad, or exposed beyond the intended purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the same flow or closely associated transaction contains both identity/account data and device identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Detailed LINDDUN Pro subtree id is approximate; linkage clearly applies to this flow.

title: The homeowner may be unaware of what personal and device data are collected during registration
description: During account registration and device enrollment, the Home Hub may collect more data than the homeowner expects, such as device metadata, network identifiers, location/timezone, or household topology. If the flow does not clearly communicate what is collected and why, the user lacks sufficient awareness.
assumptions: Assumes the registration/enrollment UX may not fully disclose all collected fields and inferred metadata.
uncertainty_note: Threat is grounded in typical onboarding flows; exact notice behavior is not specified in the prompt.

title: Registration and enrollment may occur without valid or sufficiently specific consent
description: If the Home Hub bundles account creation, device enrollment, analytics, cloud synchronization, or secondary uses into a single step, the homeowner may not be able to give freely given, specific, and informed consent for each processing purpose. This creates a non-compliance risk for the onboarding flow.
assumptions: Assumes personal data processing beyond strictly necessary account/device setup may occur, or consent capture may be inadequate.
uncertainty_note: Applies if consent is relied upon or if legal transparency/choice obligations exist; exact regulatory context is not provided.

title: The homeowner may be unable to prove or later dispute what was registered or enrolled
description: If the Home Hub does not provide verifiable records or confirmations of account creation and device enrollment, the homeowner may be unable to demonstrate which cameras/sensors were enrolled, when enrollment occurred, or what terms/notices were accepted. This can hinder dispute resolution and accountability.
assumptions: Assumes lack of receipts, audit trail visibility, or user-accessible confirmation records.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is plausible for onboarding transactions, but the existence of logs or confirmations is unknown.

title: The onboarding flow may not support homeowner control over submitted registration and device data
description: Once account and device details are sent to the Home Hub, the homeowner may have limited ability to review, correct, delete, or selectively enroll devices. Insufficient intervenability reduces the user's control over personal and household-device data processing.
assumptions: Assumes the system may not offer granular review/edit/delete options during or after enrollment.
uncertainty_note: Intervenability risk depends on available account/device-management features, which are not described.

title: Registration and enrollment may expose excessive personal or household details
description: The flow may disclose more information to the Home Hub than is necessary for basic setup, such as full household device inventory, precise device metadata, or unnecessary personal profile fields. Excessive disclosure increases privacy impact if retained, shared, or breached.
assumptions: Assumes data minimization is not strictly enforced in the onboarding payload.
uncertainty_note: Disclosure here is interpreted as unnecessary exposure of data to the receiving process; exact field set is not specified.

title: Temporary access code can be linked to a specific guest or visit
description: The temporary access code submitted by the guest may act as a persistent or unique identifier within the Home Hub, allowing the system operator or another party with access to logs to link multiple unlock attempts or visits to the same guest. Even if the guest is otherwise unnamed, the code can enable correlation of that person's interactions over time.
assumptions: Assumes temporary codes are unique per guest, booking, or visit and that the Home Hub stores or transmits them in identifiable form.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context gives applicable threat types for this interaction but not detailed LINDDUN Pro node ids.

title: Guest identity or stay details may be inferred from the temporary code
description: If temporary access codes are structured, reused, or associated with reservation records, the Home Hub's receipt of the code may allow inference of who the guest is, when they are expected, or which property/room they can access. This creates a risk that personal information is inferable from the submitted code and related metadata.
assumptions: Assumes the code format or backend association reveals or enables lookup of guest-related information.
uncertainty_note: Detailed tree node id is approximate; applicability depends on whether the code is meaningfully associated with guest records.

title: Guest may be unable to deny having entered a code at a specific time
description: If the Home Hub logs code entry events together with timestamps and code identifiers, those records can be used as evidence that a particular guest attempted or performed an unlock action. This reduces the guest's plausible deniability regarding presence at the property or participation in the access event.
assumptions: Assumes the system retains audit logs that associate code entry with a specific temporary code or guest account.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; threat depends on logging and retention behavior not fully specified in the flow description.

title: Observation of code-entry communication can reveal guest participation
description: An observer who can see that a temporary access code is being entered and sent to the Home Hub may learn that a guest is currently present or attempting entry, even without learning the code value itself. The mere existence and timing of this interaction can reveal the guest's involvement with the property.
assumptions: Assumes an attacker can observe the interaction physically, over the local network, or via visible system responses.
uncertainty_note: Grounded in the retrieved Detecting guidance, but the exact node id is approximate.

If this code is exposed in transit, displayed openly, logged insecurely, or retained longer than necessary, sensitive authentication data is disclosed. Such disclosure can also indirectly reveal guest access rights and occupancy patterns.

description: When entering a temporary access code, the guest may not understand what data the Home Hub collects, whether the code entry is logged, how long records are retained, or with whom they are shared. This lack of transparency undermines the guest's awareness of privacy-relevant processing tied to the unlock action.

title: Processing of guest access-code data may occur without an appropriate legal basis or notice
description: The Home Hub processes the guest's temporary access code and associated event data to unlock the door. If this processing, logging, or secondary use occurs without proper notice, consent where required, contractual necessity, or another valid legal basis, the flow creates a non-compliance risk. Additional compliance issues may arise if retention, minimization, or purpose-limitation obligations are not met.

description: Writing motion, door, and other sensor events into a persistent local event log creates a longitudinal record that can be linked into occupancy and behavior patterns for the same household or resident over time, even if individual events seem innocuous.
assumptions: The local event log retains timestamps and repeated events associated with the same home, device, room, or user context.

title: Local event log may reveal sensitive inferences about residents

title: Logging household sensor events may exceed consent or expected purpose

title: Uploaded clips can be linked to a specific household or resident account

This enables the cloud service to link multiple recordings over time to the same home and potentially to identifiable residents, creating a longitudinal view of household activity.
assumptions: Assumes uploads carry stable identifiers such as account ID, device ID, or authenticated session metadata, which is typical for cloud-backed video storage.

title: Cloud upload reveals sensitive inferences about occupants' behavior
description: Recorded camera clips can expose highly sensitive information such as presence at home, daily routines, visitors, interior layout, and potentially special-category data visible in footage. Even if the purpose is storage, the transfer itself makes these inferences available to the receiving cloud environment.
assumptions: Assumes the clips contain identifiable people, home interiors, timestamps, or contextual cues from which behavior and lifestyle can be inferred.
uncertainty_note: Detailed tree-node numbering is approximate; applicability of inference to this flow is high.

title: Upload discloses personal data beyond what is necessary for storage
description: The Home Hub may upload full-resolution clips, audio, rich timestamps, device identifiers, location/account metadata, and event context to cloud storage. This can disclose more personal data than strictly necessary for retaining footage, increasing privacy exposure during and after transfer.

description: Once clips are uploaded to cloud video storage, the provider may retain, index, analyze, or reuse the footage and metadata for purposes beyond simple storage, such as service improvement, analytics, model training, or law-enforcement response workflows. This creates a risk that data subjects are unaware of downstream processing.

title: Residents may be unaware that camera footage is uploaded to the cloud

This lack of awareness undermines informed expectations about where footage resides and who can access it.

title: Cloud upload of household video may lack a valid legal basis or exceed stated purpose
description: Uploading recorded home-camera clips to cloud storage may be non-compliant if the transfer is not necessary for the stated purpose, if retention and cross-border processing are not properly governed, or if affected individuals have not been adequately informed where required. The flow may therefore violate data minimization, transparency, retention, or lawful-basis obligations.

title: Excessive exposure of motion-alert data to backend
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert to the mobile app backend. If the alert contains more personal data than necessary for backend processing—such as precise timestamps, device identifiers, household identifiers, occupancy inferences, or rich sensor context—the flow may disclose avoidable personal data to another system component. Motion alerts can reveal presence/absence patterns and behavior inside the home, so unnecessary detail in this transfer creates a genuine data-disclosure risk.
assumptions: Assumes the motion alert relates to an identifiable household, user account, or device and that the backend does not strictly require all transmitted fields at full granularity.
uncertainty_note: Dd.4 is a strong fit from the provided context because the issue is excessive exposure to an involved party. Exact sub-node applicability may vary depending on the project-specific LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: Motion-alert payload may enable identification of household or user
